First, the cannabis district-court petition the review describes is gone: former Rule 1-077.1(B)(4), which created a no-filing-fee district court action under Section 29-3A-8, was deleted; Rule 1-077.1(A) now excepts cannabis records from the rule entirely; Rule 1-077.1(D) no longer names Form 4-954; and Rule 1-077.1(J) no longer refers to a Section 29-3A-8 petition. The committee commentary states the reason expressly: the amendments reflect H.B. 314, 56th Leg., 1st Sess. (N.M. 2023), which gave the Administrative Office of the Courts the verification and expedited-request procedure instead. Second, both of the review's build blockers close at source. Form 4-952 paragraph 13 requires only the New Mexico Department of Public Safety Record of Arrest and Prosecution sheet dated no later than ninety days before filing, not the FBI sheet, which resolves the review's open question on that point in the negative; Form 4-953 paragraph 16 requires both FBI and DPS sheets, so the asymmetry the review suspected is real and now confirmed. Form 4-952 paragraph 8 carries the one-year period on the face of the mandatory form, which closes the review's release blocker that the one-year wait was reference-sourced only. Third, the statutory text the review could not read was read: NMSA 1978 Sections 29-3A-1 through 29-3A-9 in full from the Supreme Court's published Criminal Record Expungement handout, Section 29-3A-4 and Section 29-3A-5 as actually amended by Laws 2021 (1st S.S.), Chapter 3 from the enacted text of Senate Bill 2, and Section 29-3A-8 as amended by Laws 2023, Chapter 74 from the enacted final text of House Bill 314. One caution recorded for the form library: the Supreme Court handout reproduces the pre-2021 Section 29-3A-4, which omits penalty assessments and Motor Vehicle Code violations and deferred sentences from the eligible list and names three parties for notice. The enacted 2021 text is broader and names two. The review is right and the handout is stale; do not let the handout narrow the eligibility list. A second caution: Rule 1-077.1(D) as approved on October 31, 2025 still contains the typographical citation to "Form 4-452 NMRA" where Form 4-952 is meant. The review found that error in a district instruction packet; it is in the approved rule itself. Form 4-452 must not enter the form library. Edition 1.2 retains seventeen New Mexico assets including Forms 4-951, 4-952, 4-953, 4-955 through 4-960.3, Form 4-222 and the DPS authorization in English and Spanish, so the review's statement that no official forms were supplied is superseded; those retained copies are the pre-amendment versions and every form identity below is taken from the October 31, 2025 approved text instead. tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Arrest Records and Public Records upon Identity Theft (NMSA 1978, Section 29-3A-3)
tracks.publicName: Clear a New Mexico record that is not yours

controllingAuthority.summary: A person wrongfully identified in arrest records or public records as a result of identity theft may petition the district court to expunge those records. On a showing that the person is a victim of identity theft the court shall order expungement and cause the order to be delivered to all relevant law enforcement agencies and courts. The proceeding is a civil petition in district court even where the underlying case was in municipal, magistrate or metropolitan court. Rule 1-077.1 supplies the procedure and its use of Form 4-951 is mandatory; the rule and every form in the set were amended by Supreme Court Order No. S-1-RCR-2024-00099, effective for all cases pending or filed on or after December 31, 2025.

exclusions: Records of another state, and federal, tribal and military records. A New Mexico district court cannot reach them.

Driving while intoxicated citations maintained by the taxation and revenue department, computer-aided dispatch information and log books relating to breath alcohol testing equipment, which Section 29-3A-2(A) excludes from the definition of arrest records.

The categories Section 29-3A-2(C) carves out of public records, including confidential arrest-record information, a district attorney or attorney general law-enforcement file, certain children, youth and families department, human services department and public education department records, and a record received through an authorized background check.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Arrest Records and Public Records upon Release Without Conviction (NMSA 1978, Section 29-3A-4)
tracks.publicName: Expunge a New Mexico case that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: One year from the date of final disposition, a person released without conviction may petition the district court where the charges originated to expunge the arrest records and public records of that case. Relief is mandatory on the findings: if the court finds no other charge or proceeding is pending and that the petitioner was released without conviction, it must order expungement. The petition is filed under seal under Rule 1-079 NMRA. Two responding parties are served by first-class mail and have sixty days to object or file a notice of non-objection; after that window the petitioner must file a notice of completion of briefing with an affirmation attached before any hearing on the merits will be set, and where no objection is filed the court may decide on the pleadings and affirmation without a hearing.

exclusions: Any case in which a conviction was entered. That is the conviction track under Section 29-3A-5.
Cases where another charge or proceeding is pending against the petitioner. The court must find there is none.
Records of another state, and federal, tribal and military records.

Driving while intoxicated citations maintained by the taxation and revenue department, computer-aided dispatch information and log books relating to breath alcohol testing equipment, which Section 29-3A-2(A) excludes from arrest records. A successful expungement on this track therefore leaves some DWI-related records untouched.
The categories Section 29-3A-2(C) carves out of public records.

rules.filing: File a civil petition on Form 4-952 NMRA under seal with the clerk of the district court for the county where the charges originated or the arrest occurred, with the DPS RAP sheet and the disposition records attached. Bring copies for yourself and for the judge and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Then mail the petition and attachments to the two responding parties and file Form 4-955 NMRA. After the sixty-day objection window closes, file Form 4-959 NMRA with Form 4-960.2 NMRA attached and serve it on any party that objected.

rules.notice: Sixty days from service for the responding parties to file specific objections on Form 4-957 NMRA or a notice of non-objection on Form 4-958 NMRA. Rule 1-077.1(G) NMRA controls over the thirty days in Section 29-3A-4(B); the committee commentary says so expressly. A party filing a non-objection is excused from further participation. A party objecting on the basis of the contents of the petitioner's FBI record of arrests and prosecutions must give the petitioner a free copy of that record at the time of filing the objection.
rules.service: Required. Service of the petition and all attachments is by first-class United States mail on the district attorney for the county in which the arrest was made or the criminal charge or proceeding was filed, and on the New Mexico Department of Public Safety. A certificate of service on Form 4-955 NMRA is then filed with the district court. Subsequent pleadings are served under Rules 1-005, 1-005.1 or 1-005.2 NMRA.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs Form 4-952 and, at the second stage, Form 4-960.2. The DPS Authorization for Release of Information must carry the participant's original signature.
rules.notarization: None required for the court filings. The DPS Authorization for Release of Information must be notarized.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The review approved this track with limitations and called it the highest-value New Mexico track: no conviction to argue about, mandatory relief on the findings, a sealed petition and a decision available without a hearing. The refresh sustains all of that on the current authority and closes both of the review's blockers. Form 4-952 paragraph 8 carries the one-year period on the face of the mandatory form, so the waiting period is no longer reference-sourced only; and Form 4-952 paragraph 13 requires only the DPS Record of Arrest and Prosecution sheet, not the FBI sheet, which answers the review's build blocker in the negative and keeps a federal records request out of this packet. The review proposed a staged or hybrid strategy. That is normalized to a single official_pdf_fill route rather than a composed one: the Rule 1-077.1(H) notice of completion of briefing is a further filing by the same petitioner in the same case to the same court under the same strategy, it obtains no relief on its own, and record gathering before it and the objection window after it are preparation and ordinary post-filing handoff. The sequence survives in the components and in the sequencing instructions.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge Arrest Records and Public Records upon Conviction (NMSA 1978, Section 29-3A-5)

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a municipal ordinance violation, misdemeanor or felony may, after completing the sentence and paying any fines or fees owed to the state for that conviction, petition the district court in the county of conviction to expunge the arrest records and public records related to it. Relief is discretionary. The court must find no other charge or proceeding pending, that justice will be served, that victim restitution ordered in connection with the conviction has been fulfilled, and that no other criminal conviction has occurred during a waiting period of two to ten years measured by offence class from the last date the petitioner completed a sentence in any jurisdiction. Five categories of offence are excluded outright. Three responding parties are served, the objection window is sixty days, the notice of completion of briefing must be filed before any hearing, and Rule 1-077.1(J) NMRA requires a hearing on this track in every case.

exclusions: An offense committed against a child. Section 29-3A-5(G).
An offense that caused great bodily harm or death to another person. Section 29-3A-5(G).
A sex offense as defined in Section 29-11A-3 NMSA 1978. Section 29-3A-5(G).
Embezzlement under Section 30-16-8 NMSA 1978. Section 29-3A-5(G).
An offense involving driving while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs. Section 29-3A-5(G).
Any conviction where the sentence has not been completed, or where fines or fees owed to the state for that conviction are unpaid. Section 29-3A-5(A).
Any case where another charge or proceeding is pending against the petitioner anywhere.

Any case where the petitioner has another criminal conviction within the applicable waiting period, measured from the last date on which they completed a sentence for a conviction in any jurisdiction.
Records of another state, and federal, tribal and military records.

components.notes: Petition to expunge arrest records and public records; upon conviction. Supreme Court approved October 31, 2025, effective December 31, 2025, read in full on 2026-08-06. Paragraph 10 is the fines, fees and restitution certification, paragraph 16 the FBI and DPS RAP sheet attachment statement, paragraph 17 the criminal-history documentation list and paragraph 18 the telephonic appearance checkbox. Notice of completion of briefing, upon conviction. Filed after the sixty-day objection period expires and served on every party that filed an objection. No hearing on the merits will be set before this filing, and on this track a hearing is mandatory, so nothing at all happens until it is filed.

Notice of hearing. Required rather than conditional on this track because Rule 1-077.1(J) NMRA requires the court to hold a hearing on a Section 29-3A-5 petition in every case. The hearing time and location are left blank because the court supplies them.

That a hearing is mandatory on this track, that relief is discretionary rather than mandatory, that the court weighs the justice-will-be-served factors, and that the district attorney may submit reasons to deny. Said up front, not at the end.

tracks.legalName: Automatic Expungement of Cannabis Arrest and Conviction Records, and the Administrative Office of the Courts Verification and Expedited-Request Procedure (NMSA 1978, Section 29-3A-8)

citations: Cannabis Regulation Act, NMSA 1978, Sections 26-2C-1 to 26-2C-42
controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person was charged with a cannabis offence that is no longer a crime on June 29, 2021, or that would have resulted in a lesser offence had the Cannabis Regulation Act been in effect, all public records held by a court or a state or local agency relating to the arrest or conviction are automatically expunged two years after the conviction date, or two years after the arrest date if there was no conviction. For a person under eighteen at the time, the records are retained for two years or until they turn eighteen, whichever comes first, and are then automatically expunged. Automatic expungement applies to public records involving only cannabis and cannabis paraphernalia charges and requires destruction of the records. The Administrative Office of the Courts must implement a procedure allowing eligible people to verify whether automatic expungement has occurred and to request expedited automatic expungement where it has not; where an arrest or conviction involved cannabis and non-cannabis charges, the person may request expungement of the eligible cannabis charges through that same AOC procedure. Requests to the AOC remain confidential and are not subject to disclosure. There is no court petition on this track: Rule 1-077.1(A) NMRA now excepts cannabis records from the expungement rule, former Rule 1-077.1(B)(4) was deleted and Form 4-954 NMRA was withdrawn, all effective December 31, 2025.

exclusions: Any offence that is still a crime under the Cannabis Regulation Act and would not have resulted in a lesser offence had that Act been in effect.
Records of another state, and federal, tribal and military records.
Anyone currently or formerly incarcerated for a cannabis offence who is seeking dismissal, vacatur or redesignation of the sentence. That is Section 29-3A-9 and it is a different track.

Non-cannabis charges within a mixed case. Automatic expungement under Section 29-3A-8(A) applies to public records involving only cannabis and cannabis paraphernalia charges; a mixed case reaches the eligible cannabis charges only through the Section 29-3A-8(C) request to the Administrative Office of the Courts, and the non-cannabis charges are left to the release-without-conviction or conviction track.

Section 29-3A-8(D) makes the request confidential and not subject to disclosure. components.notes: The whole track opens by telling the participant that the law may already have cleared and destroyed the record, that two years is the trigger, and that the correct first move is to ask the Administrative Office of the Courts whether expungement has occurred rather than to file anything. Selling a filing for a record the law already destroyed is the failure mode this ordering exists to prevent.

How to reach the Application for Expungement of Court Records involving Cannabis on the official New Mexico Courts expungement page, what it asks for, and what to have ready: full name, date of birth, the full case number, the last four digits of the social security number, an address for reply, contact details, a picture ID and any case documentation. The non-cannabis charges are not reached and are routed to the release-without-conviction track or the conviction track as applicable. This replaces the review's account, which had a mixed case partly expunged automatically.

That the district court petition on Form 4-954 NMRA no longer exists. Anyone who has read the pre-2026 New Mexico instruction packets, or the district Steps to Filing packets dated rev. 1/28/22 and rev. 7/12/22 that still describe a cannabis petition, will expect to file one. The packet must say plainly that Form 4-954 was withdrawn on October 31, 2025, effective December 31, 2025, and that the AOC procedure is the route.

That this is the one New Mexico route where records are destroyed rather than merely removed from public access; that the destruction reaches public records held by a court or a state or local agency; and that it does not reach federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records.

What to do after the AOC responds, including confirming with any agency that still shows the charge. The statute sets no response deadline for the AOC and none is published, which is recorded below as an open question.

controllingAuthority.summary: A correctional facility, county jail or juvenile correctional facility holding a person for a cannabis offence that is no longer a crime, or that would have been a lesser offence had the Cannabis Regulation Act been in effect, was required to notify the court that the case may be reopened for dismissal of the sentence or expunged. A person who has completed such a sentence is entitled to have the conviction dismissed and expunged as legally invalid, or redesignated as a penalty assessment citation. The Department of Public Safety was to identify potentially eligible past convictions and notify the corrections department, prosecutors and defence counsel, and prosecutors had until July 1, 2022 to decide whether to challenge a dismissal, expungement or redesignation. This is sentence relief and vacatur, not record clearing, and it turns on a legal-invalidity analysis.
